- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; cap forecast overshoots at +3% above immediate peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price movements by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with 1-day lagged sentiment + price momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model misreads trend; apply smoothing filter to avoid oscillation-induced overfitting.
